label: AgMsv_1.665
cite_parts:
tena svasṛṣṭe bhāvāṃśe svarūpātmany api sphuṭam /
pāratantryāvabhāso 'yaṃ devenaivāvabhāsyate // [AgMsv_1.665]
quick_english: Therefore, even in the self-created portion of being, which is essentially one's own nature, this clear appearance of dependence is manifested by the Lord alone.

tokens.grounds: part or aspect of existence; bhāva-aṃśa
whose essence is one's own nature; svarūpa-ātman

label: AgMsv_1.666
cite_parts:
pāratantryaṃ kalayati svatantraḥ parameśvaraḥ /
svātantrye pāratantrye ca nānyal lakṣaṇam ucyate // [AgMsv_1.666]
quick_english: The self-dependent supreme Lord fashions dependence; no other defining mark is stated for autonomy and dependence than this.

label: AgMsv_1.667
cite_parts:
paricchinnaprakāśo hi jaḍas tenātra yaḥ sthitaḥ /
paricchedaka eṣo 'pi paricchedyo yadi sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.667]
quick_english: For what has limited light is inert; therefore, if the limiter posited here is itself clearly something to be limited, a problem arises.

tokens.grounds: one whose light is circumscribed; paricchinna-prakāśa

label: AgMsv_1.668
cite_parts:
tad asya rūpagrahaṇe na prakāśaḥ prakāśate /
tathā hi bāhyo bhāvāṃśaḥ svayaṃ naiṣa prakāśate // [AgMsv_1.668]
quick_english: Then, in grasping its form, light does not shine; for an external portion of being does not shine by itself.

label: AgMsv_1.669
cite_parts:
jñānam arthaprakāśātma tac cānābhātam eva hi /
tasyāpi samavāyy ātmā naiva bhāti svarūpataḥ // [AgMsv_1.669]
quick_english: Knowledge is of the nature of illuminating objects, yet if it is unmanifest, even its inherent self does not shine by its own nature.

tokens.grounds: having the illumination of objects as its essence; artha-prakāśa-ātman
ca-anābhāta; not appearing; sandhi within token

label: AgMsv_1.670
cite_parts:
tadīyakaraṇaṃ netraprabhṛty api na bhāsate /
ālokādeś ca vijñānād ṛte naivāvābhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.670]
quick_english: Its instrument, such as the eye, does not shine by itself; and without consciousness there is no manifestation at all, even with light and other aids.

tokens.grounds: the instrument belonging to that; tadīya-karaṇa

label: AgMsv_1.671
cite_parts:
nanu jātaṃ yadi jñānam arthasyāsau prakāśatā /
śaktir dharmo yadi prāptaṃ sārvajñyaṃ viśvamaṇḍale // [AgMsv_1.671]
quick_english: But if, when knowledge arises, that luminosity of the object is its own power or property, then omniscience would follow throughout the whole universe.

label: AgMsv_1.672
cite_parts:
anyad evātha tat kiṃcit prakāśatvābhiśabditam /
tan meyamātṛmāneṣu naiva kutrāpi saṃgatam // [AgMsv_1.672]
quick_english: Or if that so-called luminosity is taken as something else, it does not fit coherently anywhere among the known, the knower, and the means of knowing.

tokens.grounds: designated by the term luminosity; prakāśatva-abhiśabdita
among known, knower, and knowing; meya-mātṛ-māna

label: AgMsv_1.673
cite_parts:
tataś cāprakaṭaṃ viśvaṃ sarvadaiva bhaved idam /
aprakāśasya bhāvasya yadi ca syād prakāśanam // [AgMsv_1.673]
quick_english: Therefore this whole universe would always remain unmanifest; and if an unmanifest being were to become illuminated, another difficulty follows.

label: AgMsv_1.674
cite_parts:
tāvataivāsya hīyeta svarūpaṃ parihānitaḥ /
jñānotpattiś ca bhāvasya svarūpasthasya cet prathā // [AgMsv_1.674]
quick_english: By that much its own nature would be lost; and if the arising of knowledge is the manifestation of a being while it remains in its own nature, that must be explained.

tokens.grounds: remaining in its essential form; svarūpa-stha

label: AgMsv_1.675
cite_parts:
aviśiṣṭe svarūpasthabhāve viśvasya sā na kim /
tasmāt prakāśo viśvasya paricchedakaniṣṭhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.675]
quick_english: If a being remains undifferentiated in its own nature, why would that manifestation not belong to the whole universe? Therefore the light of the universe rests in the limiter.

tokens.grounds: in an entity remaining in its essence; svarūpa-stha-bhāva
grounded in the delimiting principle; paricchedaka-niṣṭhita

label: AgMsv_1.676
cite_parts:
tatsvātantryāvabhāsotthacitrākāravibheditaḥ /
paricchedaka itthaṃ cet paricchedyo bhavet tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.676]
quick_english: If the limiter, differentiated by varied forms arising from the manifestation of its own freedom, were itself something to be limited, then a consequence follows.

label: AgMsv_1.677
cite_parts:
mūlakṣatikarī seyam anavasthā patiṣyati /
ataś ca so 'paricchinnaḥ paricchedaka ucyate // [AgMsv_1.677]
quick_english: Then this root-destroying infinite regress would occur; therefore that limiter is said to be unlimited.

label: AgMsv_1.678
cite_parts:
akālpyas tena śāstreṣu tan na kālasya gocaraḥ /
tenāsya vedyadharmatvaṃ kālasya paribhāṣitam // [AgMsv_1.678]
quick_english: Therefore it is not constructible and, as the scriptures say, not within the domain of time; for that reason the condition of being a knowable object is explained as belonging to time.

tokens.grounds: not to be conceptually fabricated; a-kalpya
the condition of having knowable properties; vedya-dharma-tva

label: AgMsv_1.679
cite_parts:
yadi kālaś ca mātāraṃ paricchindyāt tato dhruvam /
mātṛlagnaiva kālasya sthitir nirvāham icchati // [AgMsv_1.679]
quick_english: If time were to delimit the subject, then the stability of time would certainly depend on the subject and would require the subject's functioning.

label: AgMsv_1.680
cite_parts:
na ca mātrantaraṃ kiṃcit saṃbhaved anavasthiteḥ /
tāṃ hantuṃ vopagamyo 'sau mātā kālakalojjhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.680]
quick_english: And no other subject could be posited, because of infinite regress; to remove that regress, this subject must be accepted as free from the divisions of time.

label: AgMsv_1.681
cite_parts:
ya eva tu paricchedyo mātā tallagna eva cet /
sa kālo mātṛmeyatve tarhy ekasya kathaṃ tava // [AgMsv_1.681]
quick_english: But if the limited subject is indeed dependent on that time, then how, in your view, can one and the same entity be both subject and object?

tokens.grounds: in being both knower and known; mātṛ-meya-tva

label: AgMsv_1.682
cite_parts:
bhedavāde hi bhavatāṃ niṣṭhitā matir īdṛśī /
abhedavādināṃ nas tu naiva kāpy astu khaṇḍanā // [AgMsv_1.682]
quick_english: For in the doctrine of difference your view is fixed in that way; but for us, who uphold non-difference, let there be no such refutation at all.

tokens.grounds: in the view based on difference; bheda-vāda
of those who hold non-difference; abheda-vādin

label: AgMsv_1.683
cite_parts:
viśvaṃ mātṛmayaṃ yeṣāṃ mātā viśvamayas tathā /
tan na kālakalājālajambālaiḥ parameśvaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.683]
quick_english: For those for whom the universe consists of the subject and the subject likewise consists of the universe, the supreme Lord is not entangled in the mire of the nets of time and limiting factors.

tokens.grounds: by entangling nets of time and limiting factors; kāla-kalā-jāla-jambāla

label: AgMsv_1.684
cite_parts:
citiśaktiprakāśo hi mālinyam avalambate /
atas tadā saṃvṛto 'sau paścāt prakaṭarūpakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.684]
quick_english: For the light of the power of consciousness takes on a kind of tarnish; therefore it appears concealed at that time and later appears in manifest form.

tokens.grounds: the luminosity of the power of consciousness; citi-śakti-prakāśa

label: AgMsv_1.685
cite_parts:
iti tasyaiva jṛmbheyaṃ tathātvavyapadeśinī /
kalanaivāsya sā kācit svarūpāmarśanātmikā // [AgMsv_1.685]
quick_english: Thus this unfolding, which designates that condition, belongs to that same reality alone; it is a certain creative construal of its own, whose nature is reflective awareness of its own form.

tokens.grounds: consisting in reflective awareness of one's own nature; svarūpa-āmarśana-ātmikā

label: AgMsv_1.686
cite_parts:
śivayogārham ātmānaṃ yasyām ātmābhimanyate /
yato vaicitryayogena tathātmānaṃ sa manyate // [AgMsv_1.686]
quick_english: In that construal the self regards itself as fit for union with Śiva; for through connection with variety it comes to regard itself in that way.

tokens.grounds: the self takes itself to be; ātmā-abhimanyate

label: AgMsv_1.687
cite_parts:
śaktipātasya tenoktā navadhātra vyavasthitiḥ /
anyathā neśvarasyāsti rāgo dveṣo 'tha vā kvacit // [AgMsv_1.687]
quick_english: Therefore the descent of power is taught here as ninefold; otherwise the Lord would have attachment or aversion somewhere, which he does not.

tokens.grounds: of the fall/descent of grace-power; śakti-pāta

label: AgMsv_1.688
cite_parts:
yena kvāpy eṣa niyatāṃ svāṃ śaktiṃ pātayed vibhuḥ /
animittas tathā cāyaṃ śaktipāto maheśituḥ // [AgMsv_1.688]
quick_english: For if this all-pervading Lord were to send down his own power in a fixed way anywhere, that would imply a motive; thus this descent of power of the great Lord is without external cause.

label: AgMsv_1.689
cite_parts:
tena rāgakṣayāt karmasāmyāt sukṛtagauravāt /
malapākāt suhṛdyogād bhakter bhāvāc ca sevanāt // [AgMsv_1.689]
quick_english: By decay of attachment, equality of karma, weight of good deeds, ripening of impurity, union with a friend, devotion, feeling, and practice.

label: AgMsv_1.690
cite_parts:
abhyāsād vāsanodbhedāt saṃskāraparipākataḥ /
mithyajñānakṣayāt karmasaṃnyāsāt kāmyavicyuteḥ // [AgMsv_1.690]
quick_english: From practice, breaking of latencies, ripening of impressions, decay of false knowledge, renunciation of karma, and falling away of desire.

label: AgMsv_1.691
cite_parts:
sāmyāc cittasya sā śaktiḥ patatīti yad ucyate /
tad asan /
nanu tatrāpi nimittāntaramārgaṇāt // [AgMsv_1.691]
quick_english: That power descends from equality of mind is said, but that is unreal; even there another cause must be sought.

label: AgMsv_1.692
cite_parts:
anavasthātiprasaṅgasaṃbhavābhāvayogataḥ /
anyonyāśrayaniḥśreṇicakrakādyupapātataḥ // [AgMsv_1.692]
quick_english: From the absence of infinite regress and from avoiding mutual dependence, circularity, and similar faults.

label: AgMsv_1.693
cite_parts:
asmiṃs tu pakṣe sarveṣāṃ pravādānām api sthitiḥ /
yuktā sarvaṃsahe pakṣe na kiṃcit kila duṣyati // [AgMsv_1.693]
quick_english: In this view, even all doctrines have a fitting standing; in the all-enduring view, nothing is indeed faulted.

label: AgMsv_1.694
cite_parts:
yuktiḥ sudhībhiḥ svayam eva tatra śakyeta saṃyojayitum tato na /
pṛthaktayā yojanam uktam atra yad granthato vistara eṣa mithyā // [AgMsv_1.694]
quick_english: Wise ones can join it themselves there; therefore separate joining is not said here, and this textual expansion is false.

label: AgMsv_1.695
cite_parts:
upajagmur ato 'napekṣiṇīṃ śivaśaktiṃ na ca tāṃ vinā bhavet /
apavargapadaṃ yato mudhā paraśāstreṣu vimokṣasaṃkathāḥ // [AgMsv_1.695]
quick_english: Therefore they approached independent Shiva-power; without her there is no liberation-state, so liberation-talks in other scriptures are in vain.

label: AgMsv_1.696
cite_parts:
śaktipātasamaye vicāraṇaṃ prāptam īśa na karoṣi karhicit /
śrīmadutpalagurur nyarūpayat tatra tatra nijaśāstra īdṛśam // [AgMsv_1.696]
quick_english: At the time of power-descent inquiry is proper, Lord, yet you never do it; the venerable Utpala teacher showed such inquiry there in his own scripture.

label: AgMsv_1.697
cite_parts:
tasyaiva hi prasādena bhaktir utpādyate nṛṇām /
yayā yānti parāṃ siddhiṃ tadbhāvagatamānasaḥ // [AgMsv_1.697]
quick_english: By his grace alone devotion is produced in men, by which they go to supreme perfection with mind gone to his state.

label: AgMsv_1.698
cite_parts:
itthaṃ purāṇaśāstrādau śaktiḥ sā pārameśvarī /
nirapekṣaiva kathitā sāpekṣatve hy anīśatā // [AgMsv_1.698]
quick_english: Thus in the puranas and scriptures first, that supreme power is declared independent, for in dependence there is lack of lordship.

label: AgMsv_1.699
cite_parts:
kevalaṃ bhedavādāndhyasthagitālasadṛṣṭibhiḥ /
duḥsamarthatvam etasyā niyamena kvacitsthiteḥ // [AgMsv_1.699]
quick_english: Only by blind views hidden by dualism does difficulty of capacity of this power arise, by rule of its sometimes standing.

label: AgMsv_1.700
cite_parts:
paryālocyāniśaṃ karmamalasāmyaprapākataḥ /
ityādihetujāleṣu vṛthātmā parikhedyate // [AgMsv_1.700]
quick_english: Constantly considering karma, impurity, equality, and ripening in nets of such causes, the vain self is exhausted.

label: AgMsv_1.701
cite_parts:
tat teṣāṃ nopakārāya kuśakāśāvalambanam /
tasmāt sa eva tādṛkṣasvasvātantryopabṛṃhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.701]
quick_english: That is not for their benefit, like clinging to grass; therefore he indeed is endowed with such own autonomy.

label: AgMsv_1.702
cite_parts:
tadā tathā tathetyādivaicitryeṇāvabhāsate /
tad itthaṃ sarvadṛṣṭīṇām atraiva parameśvare // [AgMsv_1.702]
quick_english: Then so it appears with such variety; thus all views are right here in the supreme Lord.

label: AgMsv_1.703
cite_parts:
anupraveśa ity anyair alaṃ vā yuktiḍambaraiḥ /
tad itthaṃ devadevena svasvarūpam ihoditam // [AgMsv_1.703]
quick_english: Entry thus by others, enough, or with reasoning pomp; that own nature is here declared by the god of gods.

label: AgMsv_1.704
cite_parts:
pratyakṣaṃ tatra tanmānaṃ sarvamānadhuroddhuram /
ekam evedṛśaṃ mānam iti kecit prapedire // [AgMsv_1.704]
quick_english: Direct perception there is its measure, supreme among all measures; some held one such measure thus.

label: AgMsv_1.705
cite_parts:
dhūmād agnir iti prāyas tasyaivaitad vijṛṃbhitam /
yathā ghaṭasya pūrvāṃśadṛṣṭaikapariniṣṭhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.705]
quick_english: From smoke fire, thus mostly; this is his manifestation, as of a pot fixed by seeing its first part.

label: AgMsv_1.706
cite_parts:
mātā sphuṭāsphuṭākāratāvadarthāvalehinīm /
sphuṭām eva matiṃ matvā pratyakṣatvaṃ prapadyate // [AgMsv_1.706]
quick_english: Mother, grasping such form, having considered clear mind indeed, direct perception attains.

label: AgMsv_1.707
cite_parts:
na cānumānam antyāṃśe saṃvid ekaiva sā yataḥ /
dhūmādhyakṣapratītyantarniviṣṭāgniprathā tathā // [AgMsv_1.707]
quick_english: Not and inference in the final part; awareness is one indeed, because fire is known within smoke perception, so.

label: AgMsv_1.708
cite_parts:
ekaiva tāvad arthāṃśalehinī jāyate matiḥ /
tāvaty āṃśe sphuṭākārā pratyakṣam iti bhāṣyatām // [AgMsv_1.708]
quick_english: One indeed, so far grasping an object part, mind arises; to that extent in part clear form is direct perception, thus let it be said.

label: AgMsv_1.709
cite_parts:
yathā ratnādivaicityraṃ tathā saṃskārasaṃsthiteḥ /
netrātmamānasālokaviṣayādiṣu saṃvidi // [AgMsv_1.709]
quick_english: As variety of gems, so from establishment of impressions in eye, mind, light, object, etc., in awareness.

label: AgMsv_1.710
cite_parts:
pratyakṣam eva saṃvittau sphuṭatvenāvabhāsate /
tathā tathāvidhavyāptidhāmasaṃkārasaṃsthiteḥ // [AgMsv_1.710]
quick_english: Direct perception indeed in awareness appears as clear, so from establishment of such pervasion, light, and impression.

label: AgMsv_1.711
cite_parts:
ante tathaiva sā vittir dhūmāgnyākārarūpiṇī /
yathā ca dṛḍhasaṃskārāḥ sollekhāḥ sapadi svayam // [AgMsv_1.711]
quick_english: At the end, so indeed that awareness having smoke-fire form, as firm impressions with clear marks immediately oneself.

label: AgMsv_1.712
cite_parts:
ratnāditattvaṃ paśyanti vighnāntaratirodhitaḥ /
tathā bubhukṣitātmānaḥ śīghram evātiniścitam // [AgMsv_1.712]
quick_english: Gem etc. reality they see, obstructed by inner obstacle; so hungry selves quickly, very certain indeed.

label: AgMsv_1.713
cite_parts:
annādi gṛhṇate bhoktuṃ vyāptyādyavyavadhānataḥ /
tena pratyuktam eva syād yad āhuḥ parikalpanam // [AgMsv_1.713]
quick_english: People take food to eat without any intervening inference of pervasion or the like; therefore what the opponents call mere conceptual construction is already answered and refuted.

label: AgMsv_1.714
cite_parts:
abhyasteṣv avinābhāvasvabhāvavyāptisaṃvidaḥ /
kiṃ hi tatkalpanāvyāptivitter iti na manmahe // [AgMsv_1.714]
quick_english: In matters that have become well practiced, where awareness of invariable pervasion is already present, what use is there for a cognition pervaded by conceptual construction? We do not accept that.

label: AgMsv_1.715
cite_parts:
āśūtpattivaśād asyā na khalv asty upalakṣaṇam /
anumīyata evaṃ sā tad eva parikalpanam // [AgMsv_1.715]
quick_english: Because this cognition arises very quickly, it is not clearly noticed; so the opponent infers that it must be conceptual construction. That is the move being stated here.

tokens.grounds: what is absent due to speed

label: AgMsv_1.716
cite_parts:
aho svapakṣapātāndhāḥ svam apy upagataṃ muhuḥ /
amī vismartum ārabdhās tārkikammanyabuddhayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.716]
quick_english: Alas, these people who fancy themselves logicians, blinded by loyalty to their own side, have begun again and again to forget even what they themselves have accepted.

label: AgMsv_1.717
cite_parts:
kṣaṇāpavargiṇī buddhiḥ sarvaiva hi bhavanmatā /
utpattimātrayogena viṣayasyāvabhāsikā // [AgMsv_1.717]
quick_english: For in your own view, every cognition lasts only a moment and manifests its object simply by arising.

tokens.grounds: nature of cognition in opponent's view

label: AgMsv_1.718
cite_parts:
na kṣaṇāc cāparaṃ kiṃcid āśubhāvitvam ucyate /
tat sarvam āśubhāvy eva vijñānam iti tattvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.718]
quick_english: If swift manifestation means nothing more than what happens in a moment, then in truth every cognition would be swiftly manifesting.

label: AgMsv_1.719
cite_parts:
sarvatra bhāvajāteṣu bhaved anupalakṣaṇam /
athāvicchinnadṛṣṭīnāṃ drāghīyaḥkālagocaram // [AgMsv_1.719]
quick_english: Then non-noticing would occur everywhere among all things; or else, in the case of unbroken seeing, what is known would have to range over a longer time.

label: AgMsv_1.720
cite_parts:
jñātaṃ tenāpi tarhy artho janmamātreṇa bhāsyate /
yac cotpattivaśād eva viṣayasphuṭatātmakam // [AgMsv_1.720]
quick_english: Then even on that view the object is manifested by mere arising; and if clarity of the object is also due simply to arising, that same fact must explain everything.

label: AgMsv_1.721
cite_parts:
tasya śīghratarasthāsnubhāvo bhedāvahaḥ katham /
yat tat kila grahāpekṣaṃ svaprakāśam athāpi sat // [AgMsv_1.721]
quick_english: How can the fact that the experience is quicker make a difference, if that cognition is said to be self-luminous, even while being related to grasping?

tokens.grounds: refers to the cognition or clarity

label: AgMsv_1.722
cite_parts:
anyatropāyatāṃ yāti vidyuddīpādivat tathā /
tatraiva ciraśīghrasthabhāvo bhedāya bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.722]
quick_english: If it becomes a means elsewhere, like lightning or a lamp, then the difference between lasting long or briefly may appear right there as a basis for difference.

label: AgMsv_1.723
cite_parts:
na ca kvāpy anumāneṣu vyāptyāder grahaṇaṃ bhavet /
punaḥ punaḥ sphuṭībhāvaṃ yāti yenopalakṣyate // [AgMsv_1.723]
quick_english: And in inferences the grasping of pervasion and so on does not become clear again and again in such a way that it would be separately noticed.

label: AgMsv_1.724
cite_parts:
kiṃ ca kramikadhūmādijñānamālātmani sphuṭam /
uditāpi kathaṃ kuryād ekabhāvāvabhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.724]
quick_english: Moreover, even if a clear series of successive cognitions of smoke and so on arises, how could that produce the manifestation of a single thing?

label: AgMsv_1.725
cite_parts:
athāntyam anusandhānajñānam evaṃ kariṣyati /
tad api prāksthasaṃvittisamaṃ bhinnaṃ kathaṃ tathā // [AgMsv_1.725]
quick_english: If one says the final connecting cognition will do this, that too is distinct and just like the earlier cognitions—so how could it unify them in that way?

label: AgMsv_1.726
cite_parts:
tena prāktanavijñānamālāmanvasyate yadi /
tad asan na hi saṃdhānaṃ naṣṭāyām upapadyate // [AgMsv_1.726]
quick_english: If that final cognition is supposed to connect the earlier series of cognitions, but those earlier cognitions no longer exist, then no connection is possible once they have perished.

label: AgMsv_1.727
cite_parts:
atha smaraṇam eveha saṃdhānaṃ saṃvidāṃ bhavet /
tad apy anubhavābhāve kathaṃ nāma bhaviṣyati // [AgMsv_1.727]
quick_english: If one says that memory itself is the connection between cognitions, how could that memory arise at all in the absence of experience?

label: AgMsv_1.728
cite_parts:
na ca jñāneṣv anubhavo yujyate saṃvidaḥ kvacit /
yugapaj jñānayugalaṃ nāstīti hi bhavanmatam // [AgMsv_1.728]
quick_english: And in your view there is no pair of cognitions existing simultaneously; so an experience of cognitions by awareness does not fit anywhere in that system.

label: AgMsv_1.729
cite_parts:
jñānajñeyātmatā dṛṣṭā yugapatsthitatājuṣoḥ /
na tu pūrvāparākārasamutpannavirodhinoḥ // [AgMsv_1.729]
quick_english: The relation of cognition and its object is observed only where two factors stand together at the same time, not where they arise successively as earlier and later and are therefore opposed.

label: AgMsv_1.730
cite_parts:
tasmād vyāptyanusārāvabhāsapūrvāpi yā matiḥ /
tatrāpy akramam evedaṃ pratyakṣamānavedanam // [AgMsv_1.730]
quick_english: Therefore, even the cognition that seems to be preceded by a manifestation following pervasion is, in that very case, a non-sequential knowing of a directly perceptual kind.

label: AgMsv_1.731
cite_parts:
yathā jhaṭiti sauṣuptaprabuddhaḥ pronmiṣaddṛṣiḥ /
pratyakṣam iti bhāvāṃśadhyāmalatvanivṛtaye // [AgMsv_1.731]
quick_english: Just as someone suddenly awakened from deep sleep, with eyes just opening, acts to remove the dimness in the appearance of things, taking them directly...

label: AgMsv_1.732
cite_parts:
netrasaṃmārjanādīni vidadhannābhimanyate /
bhāvān anuminomīti tathaivātrāpi buddhyatām // [AgMsv_1.732]
quick_english: While rubbing the eyes and so on, that person does not think, 'I am inferring these things.' Let the same be understood in this case as well.

label: AgMsv_1.733
cite_parts:
yathā ca ghanasauṣuptamohāvyutthitadarśanaḥ /
svātmānam atha tatsthānaṃ vismaraty eva tat kṣaṇaṃ // [AgMsv_1.733]
quick_english: And just as someone whose vision has just emerged from the delusion of deep sleep may, for that moment, forget himself and the place he is in...

label: AgMsv_1.734
cite_parts:
atha prayatnasaṃbhāraprabuddhavimalasvadṛk /
so 'ham asmīti manvānaḥ saṃvitteḥ paramārthataḥ // [AgMsv_1.734]
quick_english: Then, when his own clear seeing is awakened through gathered effort, he recognizes, 'I am that one,' and in the ultimate sense this comes from awareness itself.

label: AgMsv_1.735
cite_parts:
tatra sarvatra nātho 'yaṃ bhairavaś citsvarūpakaḥ /
svātantryāt svaṃ vapur yāvad gūhate vivṛṇoti ca // [AgMsv_1.735]
quick_english: In all of this, the Lord Bhairava, whose very nature is consciousness, freely conceals and reveals his own form.

label: AgMsv_1.736
cite_parts:
tāvad ajñānam etasya vijñānaṃ copajāyate /
tac ca sphuṭatayā sarvapratyakṣam iti manyatām // [AgMsv_1.736]
quick_english: To that extent ignorance arises, and knowledge arises; and that knowledge, by its clarity, should be understood as directly evident to all.

tokens.grounds: of the subject or Lord's manifestation

label: AgMsv_1.737
cite_parts:
ghaṭaśabde śrute yā ca pṛthubudhnodarādidhīḥ /
tatrāpi khalu samketasmaraṇādi tathāvidham // [AgMsv_1.737]
quick_english: When the word 'pot' is heard, a cognition arises of its broad base, belly, and other features; in that cognition, convention, memory, and similar factors are present in the same way.

label: AgMsv_1.738
cite_parts:
yathā ratnaparīkṣāyāṃ svāṃ saṃvittiṃ sphuṭātmikām /
samvidantarasaṃghātais tiṣṭhati pratibodhayan // [AgMsv_1.738]
quick_english: Just as in examining a gem one awakens one's own clear awareness through assemblages of other cognitions, so that awareness stands forth distinctly.

label: AgMsv_1.739
cite_parts:
tataḥ prabuddhacaramasphuṭasaṃvittiyogataḥ /
ratnatattvaṃ vibhāty atra nopayoge 'nyasaṃvidām // [AgMsv_1.739]
quick_english: Then, through the connection with the final awakened clear awareness, the reality of the gem shines forth; at that point the other cognitions have no further use.

label: AgMsv_1.740
cite_parts:
tāḥ paraṃ tatprabodhāya kāraṇatvaṃ vitenire /
tasyaivāvabhāsayoge hi na tāsām upayogitā // [AgMsv_1.740]
quick_english: Those other cognitions exercised causality only for awakening that awareness; for in the very connection of its manifestation, they have no usefulness.

tokens.grounds: demonstrative pronoun referring to other cognitions
tasya + eva + avabhāsa + yoge, locative compound

label: AgMsv_1.741
cite_parts:
bālavaikaṭikajñānadṛṣṭāntād īdṛśāt svayam /
śābde 'pi khalu vijñāne sphuṭaivaikā prakāśadhīḥ // [AgMsv_1.741]
quick_english: From such an example as the knowledge of a child and a gem-cutter, in verbal cognition too there is indeed by itself one clear cognition of illumination.

label: AgMsv_1.742
cite_parts:
atas tathāvidhe śabde śrute yat samanantaram /
arthāvabhāsane seyam iyatī matir īdṛśī // [AgMsv_1.742]
quick_english: Therefore, when such a word is heard, whatever cognition arises immediately after in the manifestation of meaning, that cognition is of this extent and of such a character.

label: AgMsv_1.743
cite_parts:
arthaḥ sa tāvāṃs tatrāste ghaṭapūrvāparāṃśavat /
nanv asau ghaṭa ekaḥ syād avayavyātmakas tathā // [AgMsv_1.743]
quick_english: That meaning, of that extent, stands there like the prior and posterior parts of a pot. But surely that pot may be one whole composed of parts?

tokens.grounds: objection particle, sandhi form of nanu

label: AgMsv_1.744
cite_parts:
na tu śabdārthayor aikyaṃ tat kathaṃ sāmyam īdṛśam /
aho bhedagrahābhyāsatimirāvilalocanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.744]
quick_english: But there is no unity of word and meaning, so how could there be such sameness? Alas, one whose eyes are clouded by the darkness of habitual grasping of difference!

label: AgMsv_1.745
cite_parts:
sadyuktyañjanayoge 'pi na dṛṣṭiṃ vimalāṃ gataḥ /
abhinno bhagavān eṣa bhairavo bhogyabhoktṛtām // [AgMsv_1.745]
quick_english: Even with the application of the collyrium of true reasoning, he has not attained clear vision. This undivided Lord Bhairava assumes within himself the state of both the enjoyed and the enjoyer.

label: AgMsv_1.746
cite_parts:
ātmany evānusandhāya sarvadā pūrṇavigrahaḥ /
iti prasādhite pūrvaṃ kaḥ praśnasyāsya saṃbhavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.746]
quick_english: Having unified everything within himself, always full-bodied — when this has been established previously, what possibility remains for this question?

label: AgMsv_1.747
cite_parts:
tad evam upamānādāv api mānāntare sphuṭam /
saṃvitpratyakṣarūpaiva sarvatra pratibhāsate // [AgMsv_1.747]
quick_english: Therefore, thus, in comparison and in other means of knowing as well, it is clearly the form of awareness-perception alone that appears everywhere.

label: AgMsv_1.748
cite_parts:
andho 'pi sparśaśabdādyais tattadrūpaṃ vilokayan /
sphuṭatām eva tāṃ tāvat saṃvetti sa tathāvidhām // [AgMsv_1.748]
quick_english: Even a blind person, perceiving each respective form through touch, sound, and so on, cognizes that clarity of just such a kind.

label: AgMsv_1.749
cite_parts:
evaṃ jātijaḍā rūpasparśādyair abhimanvate /
sphuṭam eva hi bhāvāṃśaṃ teṣāṃ nājñātadhīḥ kvacit // [AgMsv_1.749]
quick_english: Thus those congenitally deaf apprehend an aspect of things clearly through form, touch, and so on; for them cognition is never unknown anywhere.

label: AgMsv_1.750
cite_parts:
iyaṃ lāvaṇyasarasī tāruṇyodyānakaṇḍalī /
iti tuṣyati jātyandhas tadaṅgaparimarśanāt // [AgMsv_1.750]
quick_english: Saying 'this is a lake of beauty, a shoot in the garden of youth,' a congenitally blind person is pleased from touching her limbs.

label: AgMsv_1.751
cite_parts:
aho nu sadalaṃkāraṃ gāyatīti jaḍo janaḥ /
gātur mukhaṃ vilokyaiva tāvatā parituṣyati // [AgMsv_1.751]
quick_english: Saying 'ah, he sings with ornament,' a deaf person, merely by seeing the singer's face, is satisfied by that alone.

label: AgMsv_1.752
cite_parts:
iti pratyakṣam evaikaṃ niḥsapatnaṃ vijṛmbhate /
tad asya phalacintādi kartuṃ prastūyate manāk // [AgMsv_1.752]
quick_english: Thus perception alone expands without rival; therefore a brief consideration of its fruit and so on is now begun.

label: AgMsv_1.753
cite_parts:
tad eva khalu vijñānaṃ parimarśarasātmakam /
tasmād bhedakathā naiva phalaṃ prati susaṃgatā // [AgMsv_1.753]
quick_english: That very cognition is surely of the nature of the essence of reflective awareness; therefore talk of difference is not at all well suited with regard to its fruit.

label: AgMsv_1.754
cite_parts:
hānādidhīḥ phalaṃ vāstu tasyā apy atha bhāsanāt /
yadi vā svaprakāśaiva saṃvittiḥ pāramārthikī // [AgMsv_1.754]
quick_english: Let avoidance and similar cognitions be the fruit; yet even that comes from manifestation. Or else, awareness is self-luminous and ultimate.

label: AgMsv_1.755
cite_parts:
tad eva paryanthaphalaṃ sarvatraiva suniścitam /
hlādādikaṃ phalaṃ mukhyaṃ yat sarvatreha gīyate // [AgMsv_1.755]
quick_english: That indeed is the final fruit, well determined everywhere; joy and so on, which is spoken of everywhere here as the primary fruit, is included in it.

label: AgMsv_1.756
cite_parts:
tatsvasaṃvidi viśrāntim abhyeti bharitātmani /
tad evam idam adhyakṣaṃ sarvataḥ pravijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.756]
quick_english: It comes to rest in that own awareness, in the full self. Therefore, thus, this perception fully expands on all sides.

label: AgMsv_1.757
cite_parts:
etadabhyāsaniṣṭḥasya keva siddhir na jāyate /
brahmādibhāṣitaśrautapraunmukhyena kalādikāt // [AgMsv_1.757]
quick_english: For one devoted to the practice of this, what accomplishment does not arise? Beginning from kala and so on, through an inclination toward hearing what is spoken by Brahma and others...

label: AgMsv_1.758
cite_parts:
dūrāc chravaṇavijñānam acirāt saṃpravartate /
manodṛṣṭe 'pi bhāvāṃśe sphuṭavṛttyudayo hy alam // [AgMsv_1.758]
quick_english: Hearing-cognition from afar quickly arises; even in an aspect of a thing seen by the mind, the arising of clear cognition indeed occurs abundantly.

tokens.grounds: ablative adverb, sandhi form of dūrāt

label: AgMsv_1.759
cite_parts:
svavimarśabalākrānte kiṃ citraṃ yadi jāyate /
spandaśāstre tathā coktaṃ sāvadhāne 'pi cetasi // [AgMsv_1.759]
quick_english: What wonder is it if this arises when overcome by the power of one's own reflective awareness? So it is said in the Spanda scripture, even in an attentive mind.

label: AgMsv_1.760
cite_parts:
bhūyaḥ sphuṭataro bhātīty alaṃ bahulavistaraiḥ /
itthaṃ pratyakṣam evedaṃ viśvaṃ yat parameśituḥ // [AgMsv_1.760]
quick_english: It shines forth ever more clearly — enough of much elaboration. In this way, this entire universe is indeed the perception of the supreme lord.

label: AgMsv_1.761
cite_parts:
tat tato 'py avibhinnasya mātṛvargasya tat tathā /
na ca pratītisāṃkāryaṃ tathā bhāsanayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.761]
quick_english: Even though the group of knowing subjects is undivided, there is no confusion of cognitions, because each cognition arises through its own distinct mode of manifestation.

label: AgMsv_1.762
cite_parts:
pratyakṣe 'pi same sāmyaṃ no ghaṭāghaṭasamvidoḥ /
itthaṃ pratyakṣam evedaṃ niḥsapatnaṃ vijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.762]
quick_english: Even when perception operates in the same field, the cognition of a pot and of a non-pot are not identical; thus perception itself shines forth unrivaled.

label: AgMsv_1.763
cite_parts:
tato na bhidyate cārthaḥ pratyakṣādvaitam īdṛśam /
idaṃ sandhānakalikāpariniṣṭhitabuddhinā // [AgMsv_1.763]
quick_english: For that reason the object is not divided, and such nonduality of perception is recognized by one whose understanding is firmly established in the unifying insight.

label: AgMsv_1.764
cite_parts:
ācāryanarasiṃhena pratyakṣādvaitam ucyate /
anumānapramāṇatvaṃ viśvasmin kaiś cid ucyate // [AgMsv_1.764]
quick_english: Teacher Narasiṃha teaches the nonduality of perception, while some others claim that inference is the valid means of knowing for the entire universe.

label: AgMsv_1.765
cite_parts:
tathā hi devaḥ sarvajño nirvikalpasvabhāvakaḥ /
sa cādhyakṣasvabhāvo 'pi nāyāti vyavahāryatām // [AgMsv_1.765]
quick_english: The all-knowing Lord, whose nature is nonconceptual and even perceptual, does not enter into ordinary practical usage.

label: AgMsv_1.766
cite_parts:
avikalpe vikalpātmā vyavahāraḥ kathaṃ kila /
vikalpena ca sarvo 'yaṃ vyavahāro 'vatanyate // [AgMsv_1.766]
quick_english: How could practical activity, which is conceptual by nature, arise in the nonconceptual? In fact, all ordinary practical activity is carried on through conceptualization.

label: AgMsv_1.767
cite_parts:
sa eva cānumānaṃ syāt tasyaitāḥ parikalpanāḥ /
pakṣataddharmatadvyāptitatpratītyādayo 'khilāḥ // [AgMsv_1.767]
quick_english: That very process would be inference, consisting of conceptual constructions such as the subject, its property, pervasion, and the apprehension of these, and so on.

label: AgMsv_1.768
cite_parts:
vastutas tv eka evāsau pratyayaḥ pāramārthikaḥ /
nanv adhyakṣaviyoge syād anumānaṃ kathaṃ yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.768]
quick_english: But in reality there is only one ultimate cognition. Yet one may object: how could inference exist in the absence of perception, since it depends on it?

label: AgMsv_1.769
cite_parts:
tatpratyakṣaparicchinnapratibandhanibandhanam /
satyaṃ kiṃtu ya eko 'sau devaḥ sarvajñatāspadam // [AgMsv_1.769]
quick_english: It is true that inference depends on a connection determined by perception; but ultimately that rests on the one Lord who is the abode of omniscience.

label: AgMsv_1.770
cite_parts:
tadāveśavaśād eṣā vyāptir bodhe 'vakalpate /
anyathā vahnidhūmādi tadabhāvādivedanam // [AgMsv_1.770]
quick_english: Through immersion in that Lord, pervasion becomes possible in awareness; otherwise, even relations like fire and smoke, or knowledge of their absence, could not be established.

label: AgMsv_1.771
cite_parts:
anvayavyatirekātmā na syād yugaśatair api /
ata eva hi mukhyasya mānasya sadṛśatvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.771]
quick_english: The pattern of agreement and difference would not arise even over hundreds of ages; it arises because of similarity recognized by a primary cognition.

label: AgMsv_1.772
cite_parts:
anumānam iti proktaṃ vyavahārapravartanam /
tad evam ete mātāraḥ sarvatreśvarasaṃvidam // [AgMsv_1.772]
quick_english: Inference is said to set practical activity in motion; thus all knowing subjects everywhere depend on the awareness of the Lord.

label: AgMsv_1.773
cite_parts:
upajīvitum āyānti mātṛbhāvaṃ na cānyathā /
ajño hi jantuvargo 'yaṃ kathaṃ tadaniveśataḥ // [AgMsv_1.773]
quick_english: They come to be knowers by depending on that awareness, and not otherwise; for how could this ignorant class of beings become knowers without entering into it?

label: AgMsv_1.774
cite_parts:
jñasvarūpatvam āpnoti tad vinā mātṛtā kutaḥ /
tasmād saṃvidi yogo 'sya sa ca nānena durlabhaḥ // [AgMsv_1.774]
quick_english: One attains the nature of a knower through that awareness; without it, how could knowerhood arise? Therefore this being's connection with awareness is not hard to obtain.

label: AgMsv_1.775
cite_parts:
vastuto hi na kaś cit sa savinnātho hy asau tathā /
tad evaṃ pakṣam īśānapratyakṣākṣiptavṛttikam // [AgMsv_1.775]
quick_english: In reality there is no one apart from awareness, for each knower has awareness as its lord; thus any position operates only as drawn from the Lord's perception.

label: AgMsv_1.776
cite_parts:
sāpekṣaṃ paratantre ca pāśavaṃ mānam ucyate /
ajño jantur anīśo 'yam ātmanaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ // [AgMsv_1.776]
quick_english: The bound means of knowing is said to be dependent on another; for this ignorant, non-sovereign being does not control its own pleasure and pain.

label: AgMsv_1.777
cite_parts:
īśvaraprerito yātīty ata eva munir jagau /
evam īśvarasāpekṣānumānaikapramāṇatā // [AgMsv_1.777]
quick_english: The sage declared that the being moves only as impelled by the Lord; thus, for such a being, inference dependent on the Lord is the sole means of valid knowledge.

label: AgMsv_1.778
cite_parts:
nirṇītā lolaṭākhyena guruṇā lokasaṃmatā /
anyas tadgṛhya evāha satyaṃ vādhyakṣasaṃvidaḥ // [AgMsv_1.778]
quick_english: This position was determined by the teacher named Lolaṭa and accepted by many; another thinker took it up and said, 'True, perceptual awareness also has validity.'

label: AgMsv_1.779
cite_parts:
vyavahāre 'sti mānatvam anumā tu kathaṃ pramā /
sulabhavyabhicārāyām anumāyāṃ viniścitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.779]
quick_english: In practical life, perception has validity; but how can inference be certain knowledge when error is so easily possible in it?

label: AgMsv_1.780
cite_parts:
viśaṃśramītu ko nāma parīkṣakatayā sthitaḥ /
anvayo vyatirekaś ca yaḥ sapakṣetarasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.780]
quick_english: Who, standing as a careful examiner, could rest confidently on agreement and difference, which depend on presence in similar and dissimilar cases?

label: AgMsv_1.781
cite_parts:
ādidṛṣṭas tadātve no viniścayavidhāyinau /
yais tu tasmād apāsyeta pakṣadharmādidūṣaṇāt [ṇam] // [AgMsv_1.781]
quick_english: What is seen at first does not produce certainty at that moment; therefore it should be rejected because of faults such as defects in the subject and its property.

tokens.grounds: fragmentary token as transmitted; likely part of dūṣaṇam

label: AgMsv_1.782
cite_parts:
varcaskakūṭe śuddhiṃ te kuryuḥ pāṃsukaṇoccayaiḥ /
tasmāt saṃśaya evāyaṃ pravṛttyaṅgatayā sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.782]
quick_english: They would be trying to purify a heap of filth with piles of dust; therefore inference remains as doubt, serving only as an aid to action.

label: AgMsv_1.783
cite_parts:
sa eva bhedābhāsitvān māyeti paribhāṣyate /
māyeva ca paśūnāṃ syān mānaṃ māyācidātakam // [AgMsv_1.783]
quick_english: Because it manifests difference, that same doubtful cognition is called māyā; and for bound beings, the means of knowing is māyā itself, arising from māyā and consciousness.

label: AgMsv_1.784
cite_parts:
tarko vāpy ekapakṣāṃśasthitisaṃbhāvanātmakaḥ /
arthānarthabalīyastvāt pravṛttau [ttyai] vā nivṛttaye // [AgMsv_1.784]
quick_english: Reasoning, which considers the possibility that one side may hold, serves to guide engagement or withdrawal in action by weighing the greater force of benefit or harm.

tokens.grounds: fragmentary token as transmitted; likely part of pravṛttyai

label: AgMsv_1.785
cite_parts:
prabhaviṣṇuḥ sa eveti kim anyair mānaḍambaraiḥ /
pramātā śiva evaiko yasyedaṃ svāṅgam īdrśam // [AgMsv_1.785]
quick_english: He alone is all-powerful; what need is there of other displays of means of knowledge? Śiva alone is the one knower, whose own limb this world appears as such.

label: AgMsv_1.786
cite_parts:
meyatvena samābhāti sarvato niścayātmakam /
anyaḥ punaḥ paśuḥ sarvaḥ saṃśayadhvāntamadhyagaḥ // [AgMsv_1.786]
quick_english: As an object, it appears on all sides as having the nature of certainty; but every other being, the bound soul, dwells in the midst of the darkness of doubt.

tokens.grounds: in the form of the knowable
abiding in the midst of the darkness of doubt

label: AgMsv_1.787
cite_parts:
saudāmanīdyutiprāyasaṃvitsamanurañjitaḥ /
pakṣadvitayasatyānyabhāvānyatamaniścayam // [AgMsv_1.787]
quick_english: Colored by an awareness like a flash of lightning, he reaches a certainty that one of two alternatives is true and the other not.

tokens.grounds: tinged by awareness resembling a flash of lightning
certainty of either the truth or falsity of two alternatives

label: AgMsv_1.788
cite_parts:
vindāna eva labhate nātra rūḍhiṃ kathaṃ cana /
tad evaṃ tarkataḥ sarvo vyavahāra iti sthitam // [AgMsv_1.788]
quick_english: Even while finding it, he never gains firm grounding here in any way; therefore it is established that all practical activity proceeds from reasoning.

label: AgMsv_1.789
cite_parts:
aśuddha saiva vidyeyam iti mānaṃ vidhīyatām /
aśuddhir iyatī tasyā yad vastv ananusāritā // [AgMsv_1.789]
quick_english: Let this very knowledge be designated as an impure means of knowledge; its impurity is just this, that it does not conform to the real object.

label: AgMsv_1.790
cite_parts:
anye tv anarthino nāsti pravṛttir iti niścitāḥ /
arthitvam eva sacivam ity evaṃ paryacūcudan // [AgMsv_1.790]
quick_english: But others, being certain that there is no activity for one who has no purpose, argued in this way that needfulness alone is the assisting factor.

tokens.grounds: for one who has no purpose
the state of having a purpose

label: AgMsv_1.791
cite_parts:
rāgasya mānatām itthaṃ prāhur anyātmavedinaḥ /
anye tv āhuḥ saṃśayo 'pi na nāmāniścite gaje // [AgMsv_1.791]
quick_english: Thus those who know the self as other declared that desire has the status of a means of knowledge; but others say that even doubt does not arise about an elephant that is not determined at all.

tokens.grounds: the role of a means of knowledge
those who know the self as other
nāma + aniścite fused; in what is not ascertained

label: AgMsv_1.792
cite_parts:
śaktatve sati jāyeta rāgo vāpi pravṛttaye /
tataḥ svāṃ kartṛtām īṣad ālocya janatāḥ sadā // [AgMsv_1.792]
quick_english: When there is capability, desire may arise for activity; therefore people, having slightly noticed their own agency, always engage in action.

label: AgMsv_1.793
cite_parts:
pravartanta itītthaṃ syāt kalāyā eva jṛmbhitam /
tenārthaḥ sa tathā vāstu mā vābhūt svātmanas tayā // [AgMsv_1.793]
quick_english: Thus they engage in action; this would be merely the unfolding of limited agency. Therefore, whether that object is so or not, by that power he takes himself to be an agent.

label: AgMsv_1.794
cite_parts:
manvānaḥ kartṛtām eṣa sarvatraiva pravartate /
anye tv āhur anādir yo vyavahāraḥ kriyātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.794]
quick_english: Considering himself an agent, this person engages in action everywhere; but others say that the practical activity consisting of action is beginningless.

label: AgMsv_1.795
cite_parts:
niyatiḥ saiva viśvasya pravartakatayā sthitā /
sa eva cāgamo nāma vṛddhavyavahṛtikramaḥ // [AgMsv_1.795]
quick_english: That very restriction abides as the impeller of the whole world; and that same thing is called scripture, namely the traditional course of conduct of the elders.

tokens.grounds: by being the cause of activity
the traditional course of conduct of the elders

label: AgMsv_1.796
cite_parts:
tataḥ samagra evāyaṃ dharmādipariniścayaḥ /
na pratyakṣān nānumānād bhūyasā vipralambhakam // [AgMsv_1.796]
quick_english: Therefore this complete determination of dharma and so forth does not come from perception or inference, which are for the most part deceptive.

tokens.grounds: settled understanding of dharma and so on

label: AgMsv_1.797
cite_parts:
matir abhyeti viśvāsaṃ parīkṣāpakṣaśālinām /
annaṃ kṣudhaṃ śamayate tṛṣaṃ vārīti bālakāḥ // [AgMsv_1.797]
quick_english: The mind of those inclined to examination comes to trust: children learn from others that food allays hunger and water allays thirst.

label: AgMsv_1.798
cite_parts:
anyataḥ pariniścitya tathātvānatiśaṅkinaḥ /
anyadākṣādike 'py arthe tata evādyamānataḥ // [AgMsv_1.798]
quick_english: Having ascertained it from elsewhere and not doubting that it is so, they also rely on that very source as the primary measure in other matters known by perception and so on.

tokens.grounds: not suspecting it to be otherwise
anyadā + akṣādike fused; in other matters known by perception and so on
eva + ādyamānataḥ fused; from that as the primary means of knowledge

label: AgMsv_1.799
cite_parts:
labhante niścayaṃ samyag āgamākhyāt parīkṣakāḥ /
tathā ca munir āhedaṃ puṇyaṃ pāpam iti dvaye // [AgMsv_1.799]
quick_english: Even examiners properly obtain certainty from what is declared by scripture; and so the sage said, regarding the pair, 'this is merit, this is demerit.'

tokens.grounds: from what is taught by scripture

label: AgMsv_1.800
cite_parts:
śāstraprayojanaṃ svalpaṃ nāgamasya prayojanam /
āgamo hi na nāmaiṣa pustakagranthasaṃcayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.800]
quick_english: The purpose of a teaching text is small; that is not the purpose of scripture. For scripture is not merely a collection of books and written texts.

tokens.grounds: a heap of written books and texts

label: AgMsv_1.801
cite_parts:
kevalaṃ prathitābhikhyo 'nādir vedādikaḥ kila /
kiṃ tu prasiddhir evāsau sā ca śabdasvarūpiṇī // [AgMsv_1.801]
quick_english: It is not merely the well-known, beginningless Veda and the like; rather, scripture is that established tradition itself, and that tradition has the nature of speech.

label: AgMsv_1.802
cite_parts:
yā sarvadarśaneṣv eva na jātv āyāty apohyatām /
chāgaiś caityo jaṭā bhasma bhikṣā daṇḍaḥ kamaṇḍaluḥ // [AgMsv_1.802]
quick_english: That tradition, which in all systems never comes to be rejected, includes words for goats, shrines, matted hair, ashes, alms, staff, and water-pot.

tokens.grounds: sarvadarśaneṣu + v fused in sandhi context
āyāti + y fused in sandhi context

label: AgMsv_1.803
cite_parts:
jālaṃ taptaśilā śmaśrukeśalomaviluñcanam /
agnir edhā iṣṭakaughacayanaṃ gṛhamedhitā // [AgMsv_1.803]
quick_english: Net, heated stone, plucking of beard, hair, and body hair, fire, fuel, the piling of heaps of bricks, and the householder life.

tokens.grounds: pulling out beard, hair, and body hair
the piling up of heaps of bricks
the condition of being a householder

label: AgMsv_1.804
cite_parts:
ityādisarvaśabdānāṃ prasiddhiprakramād ṛte /
ko 'bhyupāyo 'rthataḥ kḷptatadanyārthāvabodhayoḥ // [AgMsv_1.804]
quick_english: Apart from the course of established usage, what means is there for understanding, in terms of meaning, all such words and the assumed meanings of others?

tokens.grounds: of all such words and so on
from the operation of established usage
for understanding the assumed meaning and the meaning of others

label: AgMsv_1.805
cite_parts:
ittham āgama evāyaṃ pramāṇam iti dhīdhanaiḥ /
uktaṃ satyaiva vāg aiśī prasiddhir avigānataḥ // [AgMsv_1.805]
quick_english: Thus the wise have said that this scripture is a valid means of knowledge; for that established tradition is truly divine speech, since it does not deviate.

tokens.grounds: because it does not go astray

label: AgMsv_1.806
cite_parts:
prasiddha āgamo loke yuktimān athavetaraḥ /
vidyāyām apy avidyāyāṃ pramāṇam iti tat sthitam // [AgMsv_1.806]
quick_english: Whether the well-known scripture in the world is reasonable or otherwise, it is an authority in both knowledge and ignorance; thus that is established.

label: AgMsv_1.807
cite_parts:
prāmāṇyaṃ niyateḥ śrīmadbhūtajāntanivāsinām /
anye tv āhur viśeṣo 'yaṃ kālo nāmābhivartate // [AgMsv_1.807]
quick_english: For the residents of the revered Bhūtaja, authoritativeness belongs to restriction; but others say that this distinct principle operating here is called time.

tokens.grounds: validity as a means of knowledge
of the residents of the revered Bhūtaja region
nāma + abhivartate fused; operates as what is called time

label: AgMsv_1.808
cite_parts:
sphuṭabhāvasvabhāvo 'sau vartamāno 'bhivartate /
vṛttasphuṭasvabhāvāṃśas tadā tv asphuṭatāmayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.808]
quick_english: That present time operates with the nature of clear manifestation; but then it has an aspect whose clear nature belonged to the past and is now marked by non-clarity.

tokens.grounds: having the nature of a clearly manifest state
having a part whose nature was clearly manifest in the past

label: AgMsv_1.809
cite_parts:
bhūtaḥ kāraṇakḷptyā tu bhāvy asau parikalpyate /
sa cāyaṃ na svatantro 'sti kaś cid anyonyasaṃśrayāt // [AgMsv_1.809]
quick_english: The past is conceived through the assumption of a cause, while the future is conceived as what is to come; but neither of these is in any way independent, because they depend on each other.

tokens.grounds: what is to be, future time
because of relying on each other

label: AgMsv_1.810
cite_parts:
anavasthānato rūpaparāvṛttyavalokanāt /
iyattārūḍhyabhāvāc ca mātṛmeyobhayāśrayāt // [AgMsv_1.810]
quick_english: Time cannot stand independently because it leads to infinite regress, because forms are seen to reverse, because it has no fixed measure, and because it depends on both the knower and the known.

tokens.grounds: because of lack of stable stopping point
because form is observed to turn back or change
because no determinate limit is established
because it relies on both knower and known

label: AgMsv_1.811
cite_parts:
nirupādhikatadrūpapratibhānaviyogataḥ /
ekānekadhruvānityasvarūpānupapattitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.811]
quick_english: Time has no coherent nature of its own, because it never appears without conditions and because it cannot be consistently established as one or many, permanent or impermanent.

tokens.grounds: because its form never appears without limiting conditions
because its nature cannot be coherently one, many, permanent, or impermanent

label: AgMsv_1.812
cite_parts:
ekasyaikopadher aikyāt tirodher (?) upadherapi /
kriyāyāḥ svagate bhede kālasyānupayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.812]
quick_english: If a single thing has a single limiting condition, its unity does not require time; and if difference belongs to action or to the condition itself, that is explained internally, so time serves no purpose.

tokens.grounds: for one thing with one condition
because time serves no explanatory role

label: AgMsv_1.813
cite_parts:
tatkṛte 'nyonyasaṃśrityānyakṛte 'py anavasthiteḥ /
aupādhikabhidāvṛtter asatyatvād avāstavāt // [AgMsv_1.813]
quick_english: Whether difference is produced by time itself or by something else through mutual dependence, the result is infinite regress; and since such conditioned difference is unreal and unsubstantial, it cannot establish time as truly real.

tokens.grounds: if produced by something else while mutually dependent
because no stable stopping point is reached
because difference arises only through conditions
because it is not ultimately real

label: AgMsv_1.814
cite_parts:
kāryasyānupapattitvād ekasyānupayogataḥ /
citaś ca sphuṭatādattavartamānasadātvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.814]
quick_english: Because time cannot be established as an effect and a single undivided thing does not need it, the clear sense of the present and its enduring presence are given by consciousness itself.

tokens.grounds: because a produced effect cannot be established
because a single undivided thing serves no temporal function
because consciousness bestows vivid presentness and enduring presence
